title: Supply Chain
tagline: Code travels from a developer's commit to production through a build system and a registry. At each hop: can you show where this came from?

client.name: Developer
client.brief: Writes the change and says what should be built.

application.name: Build System
application.brief: Turns a commit into an artifact, and signs a statement of how it did so.

idp.name: Registry
idp.brief: Stores artifacts and hands them out. Decides what it will accept.

mcp.name: Deployer
mcp.brief: The last gate before production. Decides what is allowed to run.

teaches: An artifact is only as trustworthy as the account of where it came from. Provenance is that account, signed by the builder.
Names and tags can be moved. A digest can't: it is the content.
Every hop can verify what it was handed. Nothing forces it to, and an attacker needs only one hop that didn't.

glossary.means: A signed statement from the build system: this artifact was built from this commit, by this pipeline.
A fingerprint of the artifact's exact bytes. Change one byte and the digest changes.
The exact version and digest of every dependency. A build that follows it gets the same inputs every time.
A public, append-only record of signatures. A signature that isn't in it could have been made in secret.
A public package that shares a name with an internal one, and gets installed in its place.
A list of everything inside an artifact, so you can ask what is affected when a flaw is announced.
